attacks.attack: 1. Corrupt k-1 witnesses and witness a lie
attacks.detail: 3 corrupted witnesses on a forged root -> witnessed=False. The honest margin holds until the k-th corruption.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — below k, a forged root is not witnessed

attacks.attack: 2. Corrupt k witnesses + control selection (no honest asked)
attacks.detail: 4 corrupted witnesses, no honest witness in the asked set -> witnessed=True. The margin is exactly k; raising it (independence, staking, who-pays) is gate G3, and a SILENT takeover also requires controlling who is asked.
attacks.verdict: ACCEPTED LIMIT — break cost is k independent corruptions + selection control (G3)

attacks.attack: 3. k corrupted but an honest witness is still asked
attacks.detail: equivocation conflicts=1. With >=1 honest witness in the asked set, the forged root and the true root collide and are flagged.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — one honest witness exposes the fork

attacks.detail: 4 unregistered fake witnesses -> valid=[], witnessed=False. Reaching quorum from outside the registry is impossible; biasing SELECTION among registered witnesses is the disclosed limit (needs independent selection).
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — the pinned registry rejects unregistered witnesses

attacks.attack: 5. Liveness DoS: take witnesses offline below k
attacks.detail: only 3 witnesses online (< k) -> witnessed=False (un-witnessed). Safety holds (never falsely witnessed); liveness is traded away — the layer would rather produce nothing than a falsely-witnessed root.
over-claim hits: none; discloses k-corruption margin: True; discloses liveness-not-guaranteed: True.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — discloses the k-corruption margin, selection-control, and liveness limits
